findings.claim: The machine-specific path verifier still misses Windows user-profile paths written with forward slashes.
findings.evidence: The refiner constraint/evidence claims Windows-profile absolute paths are rejected, but `findMachineSpecificPath` only matches Windows profiles with `/[A-Za-z]:\\Users\\[^\\\s"'`]+(?:\\|$)/i`; a common portable-config form like `C:/Users/alice/project/file.ts` does not match unless it also contains a Flint repository name.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the Windows user-profile pattern to accept both separators, e.g. `/[A-Za-z]:[\\/]Users[\\/][^\\/\s"'`]+(?:[\\/]|$)/i`, and add a `C:/Users/...` regression.

findings.claim: The JWT service-role scanner only inspects tokens whose header starts with `eyJ`, so valid compact JWTs with a JSON header serialized with leading whitespace can bypass value-level credential detection.
findings.evidence: The security boundary requires service-role JWT values to be rejected, but `containsServiceRoleJwt` extracts candidates with `/(?<![A-Za-z0-9_-])eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]*\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]*(?![A-Za-z0-9_-])/g`; a valid JWT header such as ` {"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT"}` base64url-encodes to a token not beginning with `eyJ`, so its `role: "service_role"` payload is never decoded.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract generic base64url compact-JWT triplets with delimiter lookarounds, decode and JSON-parse the header and payload, and reject service-role claims regardless of the header segment prefix.
